rows.wylie: kho na re, yid kyi rnam shes zag med kyi shes rab kyi 'khor du smos pa mi 'thad de, sems byung las sems gtso che ba'i phyir zhe na, skyon med de, spyir de ltar yin yang chos rab tu rnam 'byed kyi skabs su shes rab gtso che ba yin pa'i phyir, dper na, yid ches pa'i gnas skabs na dad pa gtso che ba bzhin no
rows.english: Someone may object that it is improper to speak of consciousness of one's thoughts as being "attendant" to unstained wisdom, since mind itself must be considered more primary than mental functions. Generally the relationship is so, but in the context of an ultimate analysis of phenomena wisdom must be treated as the more primary. If the context had been the subject of belief, for example, we could even have considered faith more principal.

rows.english: Someone might now make the following claim: In this situation, there does exist some real water there. This is because the human can confirm the water with his own experience, as it performs all the functions of water--as he uses it to wash himself, or as he uses it to cook something. Well then, in the same situation there must exist some real pus and blood there as well, because in this same situation the craving spirit can confirm the pus and blood with his own experience as they perform their functions--as he drinks them, and then as the sizzle in his throat and stomach, and so on.

rows.english: Someone might make the following claim: Isn't it true that when all those beings sit down together and look at something, there isn't any actual pus and blood at all? Because isn't it true first of all that, when a person with cataracts looks into a porcelain basin, there is no strand of hair in the basin at all? And, secondly, doesn't [Master Dharmakirti's] text itself say, Identical to the case of someone where his sense power has a cataract, Is the mind of a craving spirit as well, which sees a stream of water as pus.

rows.wylie: 'di la kho na re, de 'dra ba'i mtshan med kyi rnal 'byor de sgom stobs kyis stong nyid mngon sum du rtogs pa'i tshe yang bzhin lag gi rnam pa can gyi lha'i sku snang bar thal, khyod kyi dam bca' 'thad pa'i phyir na ma khyab ste, kun rdzob pa'i lha'i sku mi snang yang rgyud gyi sgo nas lha'i rnal 'byor du 'jog pa'i phyir
rows.english: At this point, someone might come and raise the following issue-- Suppose one does perform this deep practice where there are no more signs, as you've described it above, and then due to this meditation they manage to perceive emptiness directly.  Wouldn't the precious body of an Angel, complete with face and arms, be coming up in their mind at the very same time?  Because isn't your own position, in fact, correct? To this we answer, "It doesn't necessarily follow."  Because even though the precious body of an Angel which belongs to deceptive reality isn't in fact coming up in their mind at that point, we can still say that they are engaged in the deep practice of an Angel, as this practice is considered over a continuous length of time.

rows.wylie: yang kho na re, lta ba dang rgod pa sogs las byung ba'i bde ba gsum gyis stong nyid rtogs pa med par thal, de dag lam du byed pa ni stong nyid rtogs pa'i yul can khyad par can skyed pa'i don du ma yin pa'i phyir zer na dpyad par bya ste, rjes 'jug phal cher gyis de 'dra yod par bshad kyang , rje bdag nyid chen po'i legs bshad rnams su de ltar gsal bar gsungs pa'i shes byed yod med tshol dgos pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: In response to all this, someone else may come and say, Are you saying then that we don't use the three different kinds of pleasure that we feel from looking into each other's eyes, flirting, and the rest to perceive emptiness?  Because you have stated that using these as a path is not something which is done in order to give rise to the extraordinary state of mind which perceives emptiness. Our reply is that this is a question which needs to be looked into further.  Later generations of writers have, for the most part, expressed the opinion that in those classes of teachings the pleasure is used in that way.  We have to see though whether or not in the high writings of the Lord himself there is any clear statement that this is the case.
